pr_title: subsys: pm: Fix cpus active count
pr_body:
Only set a cpu as active (on pm subsystem) when the cpu is effectively initialized. We cannot assume on pm subsystem that all cpus were initialized since when the option CONFIG_SMP_BOOT_DELAY is used cpus are initialized on demand by the application.

Note that once cpus are properly initialized the subystem is able to track their status.

Fixes #58502
pr_comments:
While I think I agree with either @andyross or @gmarull in that the co-dependency here needs solving, this is a bug fix, solving a problem.

Refactoring to fix the dependencies here can be done in the 3.5 timeline.

> I think the solution should be the other way around: PM can subscribe to Kernel, so that when a CPU is initialized, PM subsys is notified and can do the appropriate actions. This way we keep subsystems isolated.

What exactly you propose ? Right now we have no thread on pm subsys that we could use to subscribe for kernel events (that also would requires an additional event)  or other mechanisms like messages queue, pipes or whatever.  Also, is not something can be done in an initial service through `SYS_INIT` (kernel keeping count of cpus) since CPUs can be brought up asynchronous.
Adding a new API where the kernel keeps callbacks to be called when CPUs are activated is possible but will introduce overhead for this specific thing (also this will not be necessary if we move pm into kernel). I think the right direction will be moving the pm subsystem into the kernel, but I think is way to risky doing it now.

Not that kernel calling pm subsystem already exists, it is not something new.

Just to be clear, I agree with @gmarull and @andyross I just don't see a better solution for this bug fix now.

Honestly given that the only user is a single global subsystem which is inherently tied to the kernel anyway, I think I'd prefer the code as originally written.  I was only complaining about the directory location and the API layering hygiene.  But I wouldn't NAK either trick.

Dynamic runtime pubsub/listener/handler registration is sort of Not The Zephyr Way, we've always preferred build time complexity to runtime behavior.

> Honestly given that the only user is a single global subsystem which is inherently tied to the kernel anyway, I think I'd prefer the code as originally written. I was only complaining about the directory location and the API layering hygiene. But I wouldn't NAK either trick.
> 
> Dynamic runtime pubsub/listener/handler registration is sort of Not The Zephyr Way, we've always preferred build time complexity to runtime behavior.

If runtime complexity is the problem, we can use iterable sections so everything is sorted at compile time. To me, creating such inter dependencies is just a bad design, and we should do better if we can.

In the abstract, sure.  But between **runtime power management** and the kernel?  Meh.  It's basically the kernel already, at least at this level.  That was what I was getting at upthread: maybe we should separate the device model side of PM from the kernel stuff; the former is reasonably a "subsystem", the latter not so much.

> > Honestly given that the only user is a single global subsystem which is inherently tied to the kernel anyway, I think I'd prefer the code as originally written. I was only complaining about the directory location and the API layering hygiene. But I wouldn't NAK either trick.
> > Dynamic runtime pubsub/listener/handler registration is sort of Not The Zephyr Way, we've always preferred build time complexity to runtime behavior.
> 
> If runtime complexity is the problem, we can use iterable sections so everything is sorted at compile time. To me, creating such inter dependencies is just a bad design, and we should do better if we can.

It is not creating any new dependency @gmarull. The kernel already does calls to subsys/pm. There is no discussion about this inter dependency, I will work to properly fix it. The point here is that make it more complex will not break this already existent dependency and will probably be reverted when we move it to the kernel.

@gmarull @andyross Just moved the variable to inside the kernel, this avoids including private headers from PM subsys and calls from kernel to pm (only for this case). Are you ok with this implementation ?

issue_context.title: pm: Subsystem is not keep tracking of active cpus correctly
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The power management subsystem is assuming that all cores are activated during the boot. This is not correct, since
if the target is built with `CONFIG_SMP_BOOT_DELAY=y` only the first core is activated during the boot.

The consequence of this change is that when the power management is suspending a cpu it may wrongly assume that
there are other cores still active and not suspend devices.

**To Reproduce**

1. Build a multicore target with:
```
CONFIG_PM=y
CONFIG_PM_DEVICE=y
CONFIG_SMP_BOOT_DELAY=y
```
2. Do not start another core (`z_smp_start_cpu`)
3. Devices will never be suspended


**Expected behavior**

CPUs should be consider active only after their be started and consequently when the last cpu is suspending, devices should be suspended.

**Impact**

PM not working properly and devices never called to suspend.

review_comments: Probably want this underneath CONFIG_MP_MAX_NUM_CPUS > 1, but one word of storage is minor.  Could also move it to the kernel struct and maybe put it under an API for use in PM, but that's minor and we can clean things up whenever.
